data.title: The Slavic sanctuary at Most pri Bratislave in two new drawings
data.excerpt: Our collaborator Haden Sutton has drawn two original views of the Slavic pagan sanctuary discovered at Most pri Bratislave – so far the only one archaeologically proven in the territory of present-day Slovakia. Dated to the 8th century, it belongs to the time when Christianity was beginning to spread while the local population still worshipped its own pagan gods.

children.text: We are very glad to be able to bring our readers two more original drawings of the life of our Slavic ancestors. This time they were drawn for us by our collaborator Haden Sutton, who took on the difficult task of drawing the Slavic sanctuary that was discovered at

This is so far the only archaeologically proven Slavic pagan sanctuary in the territory of present-day Slovakia. We date it to the 8th century, that is, to the period when Christianity was beginning to spread here, when the local population still worshipped its own pagan gods. Haden made a detailed study of the plan and of the reconstruction drawing of the sanctuary, and on their basis he tried to create two drawings of the sanctuary as seen by its visitors, who had come to pay homage to the Slavic gods.
